title: Four-Week Content Gap Heatmap
model_settings: Thinking level Standard; picker showed Selected 3.5 Flash All-around help before prompting.
continuation_reasons: Prompt 2 repaired v1 inline onclick, dynamic innerHTML/template rendering, and unsafe user/content markup paths caught by static review.

primary.title: Get Monthly Content Calendar In 1 Click
primary.use: Demand signal only: marketers want a quick month of content ideas and planning coverage without staring at a blank calendar.

secondary.title: PromptBase marketplace
secondary.observed_surface: Marketplace-style surface with Trending/Most Popular sorting and Marketing/Social/Plan categories; no individual card metrics loaded in the text view.
secondary.use: Reinforced demand for productized marketing planning prompts, but no PromptBase prompt text or metrics were copied.

pathforge_fit_adaptation: The outside prompt demand was altered from an AI monthly-calendar generator into a deterministic local heatmap editor: users enter pillars, channels, and key dates, then place content across four weeks to reveal empty stretches, repetition, overstuffed days, and missing CTA/format coverage. It is self-contained/offline because PathForge artifacts need to run without hosted AI calls, remote fonts, CDN assets, external APIs, or multi-file bundles.
final_artifact_clue: Final artifact title: 4-Week Content Heatmap Planner; verified 28 calendar day cards, diagnostics, sample data, safe pasted-text rendering, and no 390px overflow.

artifact_versions.notes: First real artifact. Rejected for inline onclick, dynamic innerHTML/template rendering, and unsafe user/content markup paths.
First repair artifact. Dynamic card rendering was safer, but static scan still found innerHTML container-clearing calls.
Second repair artifact. Static safety scan passed, but local browser verification measured horizontal overflow from the calendar grid.
Final verified artifact. No external resources or unsafe dynamic HTML sinks detected; desktop and 390px overflow checks passed.

verification_notes: Pre-provider guards passed: npm run check:source-run-intake and npm run check:hourly-seed-manager.

Final static scan passed: no http/https URLs, CDN scripts/styles, remote fonts, script src, stylesheet links, inline event attributes, innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, or document.write in final artifact.
Final inline script parsed with new Function().

Chrome localhost workflow passed: artifact loaded with 28 day cards and 4 diagnostics; scheduling a post updated day 6 and diagnostics; hostile-looking title Promo push rendered as literal text with imageCount 0.
Desktop overflow repair passed after prompt 4: document scrollWidth/clientWidth and body scrollWidth/clientWidth both 1405px in Chrome.
390px same-origin iframe harness passed: frameClientWidth 390, artifact document scrollWidth/clientWidth 375, body scrollWidth/clientWidth 375, 28 day cards, 4 diagnostics.
Temporary 390px harness was deleted after measurement; it is not part of the package.

recommended_seed_profile.registry_precheck: No pathforge-seed-163, LilaHart, or Lila Hart entry found before package creation.

goal_tracking.objective: Produce the Gemini Four-Week Content Gap Heatmap source-run package with a one-prompt preference, evidence-backed repair only for verified defects, exact-source capture, local artifact verification, package/reject output, and Chrome cleanup.

pass_reason: Final artifact is a useful offline mobile-safe four-week content heatmap editor with exact source evidence, preserved artifact versions, safe rendering, no external dependencies, no horizontal overflow at 390px, and complete provider/model/profile metadata.

steps.prompt_exact: I need a small browser tool I can save and open on my phone to plan four weeks of marketing content: let me enter campaign pillars, channels, and key dates, tap or drag posts onto a calendar heatmap, and quickly spot empty stretches, repeated formats, missing CTAs, and overstuffed days.
steps.response_summary: Gemini returned a complete four-week content heatmap HTML tool, but it used inline onclick and dynamic innerHTML/template rendering for user/content data.
